- `--lane-run-id <id>` — required stable lane identity, shared with the
  metering manifest (`CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` is the environment form).
- `--suite-status <path>` — required JSON object keyed by milestone. Every
  selected segment must have `{ "pass": boolean, "receipt": string|null }`.
  The runner validates this complete linkage before credentials, Playwright,
  receipt creation, or browser startup. A passing value must carry a non-empty
  suite evidence pointer in `receipt`. Receipt paths are relative to the
  suite-status file, must remain under its directory, and are statted and
  SHA-256 digested before startup. The digest is retained in the segment
  summary so the meter can detect a change when it writes the record.
- `--adapter <path>` — optional lane navigation/fixture adapter. It carries
  route paths and fixture choices only; it cannot report outcomes or bypass
  browser observations. The built-in adapter uses `/profile/{handle}`,
  `/profile/edit`, `/settings`, `/search`, and `/insights` plus the committed
  fixture pack. `routes.insights` may override the M8 Insights route.
- `--simulator-status <path>` — optional separately recorded M6/M8 simulator
  statuses. A single legacy status object is accepted, as is a bundle keyed by
  `m6` and/or `m8`; entries use `{ "id":"ios-simulator-m6"|
  "ios-simulator-m8", "pass":true|false|null, "receipt":string|null,
  "reason":string|null }`. Each entry is retained only in its matching summary
  and never gates web green; see `simulator.md`.
- `--timeout <ms>` — positive integer timeout for ordinary UI observations;
  default `10000`. The M3 2-second appearance and 5-second expiry ceilings are
  fixed by the brief and are not relaxed by this flag.
- `--help` — print usage without loading Playwright.

Exit code `0` means every selected segment has `green:true` (suite plus complete
required choreography). Exit code `1` means execution completed but at least one
segment was not green because a required check was skipped, an implemented
check failed, or suite evidence was absent/failing. Exit code `2` is
configuration or fatal harness failure.

## Environment variables

- `CHOREO_BASE_URL` — required lane web URL.
- `CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` — required stable lane identity unless
  `--lane-run-id` is supplied.
- `CHOREO_PASSWORD` — shared fixture password fallback for Alice, Bob, and Carol;
  Alice's M8 second context uses the same Alice credential.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_PASSWORD`, `CHOREO_BOB_PASSWORD` — per-persona passwords;
  `CHOREO_CAROL_PASSWORD` is also required for M5 unless the shared fallback is
  set. Passwords have no CLI flags so
  they do not appear in the process command line.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_BOB_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_CAROL_EMAIL` — optional;
  defaults are the corresponding `@example.com` personas from `CONTRACT.md`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER` — default for `--browser`.
- `CHOREO_RECEIPTS` — default for `--receipts`.
- `CHOREO_OBSERVATIONS` — default for the typed assertion-wait sidecar.
- `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS` — default for `--suite-status`.
- `CHOREO_ADAPTER` — default for `--adapter`.
- `CHOREO_SIMULATOR_STATUS` — default for `--simulator-status`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` — optional browser executable path for runners
  using a system Chromium/Chrome with the Playwright protocol package.
- `CHOREO_TIMEOUT_MS` — default for `--timeout`.

CLI values override their environment defaults. `--headed` has no environment
alias.

## Segment coverage after P2 hardening

Implemented checks make real UI observations and fail normally
when the lane does not satisfy them:

- M1: display-name/bio edits appear on the other client live; session survives
  reload; logout remains signed out across reload.
- M2: live text-post delivery, follow/unfollow Following projection, author
  display name on `sm-feed-item`, live like/unlike count, repost attribution
  and removal, follow-edge vs viewer-repost disambiguation on Following, and
  reply count/thread projection. Live checks run all three trials.
- M3: live DM text on `sm-convo-bubble`, typing visibility within 2 seconds
  and expiry within 5 seconds, plus quoted excerpt and jump behavior through
  the excerpt-only `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector. Live checks run
  best-of-three.
- M4: photo render, video playback, reaction set/replace/remove, edit visibility,
  and delete-for-everyone tombstones across the isolated Alice/Bob contexts.
- M5: group color/background synchronization to Carol, view-once first/second
  view behavior, warm-offline search, and shortened-window disappearing purge.
- M6 web: two offline messages expose pending state, reconnect, arrive exactly
  in order, and reach read receipts.
- M8 web: Bob's like increments Alice's refreshed Insights total; a second
  Alice context receives a same-account message live; opening the conversation
  on Alice client 1 clears `sm-chats-unread` on client 2; and two warm-offline
  Alice clients each queue a message, reconnect in an observed server-arrival
  order, converge without duplicates, and reach normal read receipts.

Remaining unsupported assertions are emitted as `status:"skipped"`, with
`pass:null`, a reason, and whether they are required. Required skips keep the
segment non-green; optional skips are visible but do not masquerade as failures:

- M2 image/video composition (no compose media-picker test ID).
- M2 feed-author avatar (no feed-avatar test ID; display name is required).
- M3 sender-avatar (no sender-avatar test ID; live DM text is required).
- M3 semantic sent/delivered/read tokens (`sm-convo-receipt` exists, but
  glyph/color inference is not an honest state-machine proof).
- M3 group aggregate-receipt and member-removal/history (no group-member
  lifecycle controls in the frozen contract).

The hardening extends the coordination contract for semantic controls and adds
a frozen route/fixture adapter for the four places where navigation cannot be
inferred from a component test ID. The adapter is input-only; the browser still
performs and observes every check.

## Receipts and green aggregation

Each assertion prints one line beginning `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` and appends the
raw JSON object to the JSONL file. Timing-sensitive assertions always retain all
three attempts. A per-segment summary follows its assertions.

See `receipts-format.md` for field meanings and `receipts.schema.json` for the
machine schema. Milestone green is fail-closed:

```text
green = suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true
```

Segment summaries also emit `nonGreenCause` (`null` when green; otherwise
`suite-failed` | `choreography-failed` | `required-unimplemented` |
`instrument`). The field remains optional on the schema since `0.3.1-m8` (default
`null`); the emitter always writes it. Prior `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain
governed by their matching schema revision. Lanes MUST copy that field into
the run record. Do not invent a second green label such as "functionally
green".

M6 and M8 web green are intentionally distinct from their simulator artifacts.
`simulator.md` remains the native proof contract; each matching status is
recorded under `choreography.supplementalExternal` and scored as native/O4
evidence rather than silently making web milestones unreachable.

## 0.3.3-m8 migration

`0.3.3-m8` is the coordinated observability bump for LLP 0295 R2. Runners
MUST pass `--suite-status` (or `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS`) and the file MUST contain
an entry for every selected segment. Missing or partial linkage exits `2`

`green:false` instrument result. Run records retain the input and suite
receipts in the additive `socialMessenger.suiteStatusLinkage` block.

The same instrument pin adds additive, hash-linked D0.6 milestone fields for
semantic actions, failure-to-recovery episodes, restart/reseed counts, browser
assertion waits, host load, and API interruptions. The run-record extension
stays at version `2` for old-record compatibility; current records must carry
`instrumentVersion: "social-messenger@0.3.3-m8"` and must carry each block as
either claimed or explicitly non-claimed. Browser waits have independent
`suite` and `choreography` owners: this executable claims only choreography,
while the production lane controller records actual suite settlement waits.
The W2 five-counter
native-usage channel is unchanged, while its meter now verifies and joins the
typed observation sidecars.

`0.3.2-m8` uses the unambiguous `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector as the sole

# Social-messenger fixture pack

Version: `0.2.0-m8`

Provenance: LLP 0201 D7 P1 — the canonical `social-messenger` benchmark's
fixture-pack prerequisite.

This directory is the backend-neutral data and media pack for Clique. Replay
adapters consume action logs through an application's real authentication and
mutation paths; the logs are not database imports.

## Artifacts

- `action-schema.md` and `action-schema.json` freeze the action-line grammar,
  all 13 verbs, checkpoint markers, idempotent set-state arguments, and the
  settle-before-next rule.
- `personas.json` contains the eight starter accounts, their fixed passwords
  and complete profiles, plus the `u0001`–`u1000` scale naming and credential
  rule.
- `starter-m1.log`, `starter-m2.log`, and `starter-m3.log` are the committed
  milestone segments. M1 has only registrations and profiles; M2 adds the
  intentionally asymmetric follow graph and post corpus; M3 adds one DM, one
  group, messages, and quoted replies.
- `sample-50.log` is the committed M6 replay-adapter conformance sample. It has
  exactly 50 actions and exercises every verb at least once.
- `invariant-manifest-starter.json` describes the exact state after all three
  starter segments. `invariant-manifest-combined.json` describes the exact
  starter-plus-scale state, per-chat counts, per-user follow/conversation
  counts, named spot content, the O5 fixtures, and the 10%/50% checkpoint
  sub-manifests.
- `scale-log.sha256` pins the derived scale log. The scale log itself is not
  committed; its line and action counts are pinned in the combined manifest.
- `config/digest.production.json` schedules one digest period per day, anchored
  at 08:00 UTC. `config/digest.shortened.json` schedules one period every 2
  minutes for grading. Both configs require at most one digest per user per
  period and server-authoritative schedule evaluation.
- `config/windows.production.json` carries 15-minute edit, 60-minute
  delete-for-everyone, and off/24-hour/7-day disappearance values.
  `config/windows.shortened.json` freezes grading values at 1 minute, 2
  minutes, and off/3 minutes/5 minutes respectively while retaining the
  production option identities.
- `media/` contains six labeled 640×480 PNGs, two labeled 256×256 avatars, one
  five-second 320×240 H.264/AAC MP4, the deterministic generator, and an
  adjacent content-hash manifest.

## Named scale fixtures

- `u0500` follows exactly 500 accounts and belongs to exactly 100
  conversations; `u0005` is the existing 5-follow comparison account.
- `u0900` is the celebrity: exactly 900 scale users follow it, and it authors
  exactly 200 top-level posts spread evenly through the scale log.
- `u0901` is the celebrity-follower read-path probe. It follows exactly
  `u0001`, `u0002`, `u0003`, `u0004`, and celebrity `u0900`.
- `g0001` remains the 50-member busy group with exactly 10,000 messages.

The combined manifest records these fixtures at the 10%, 50%, and final
states; celebrity post counts at those states are 20, 100, and 200.

## Regeneration

Run from this directory with Node.js and `ffmpeg` available:

```sh
node generate.mjs starter
node generate.mjs sample
node media/media-gen.mjs
node generate.mjs manifests
```

The manifest command recomputes the starter state and refuses any drift from
the committed starter manifest before writing the combined manifest. Additive
fixture milestones therefore retain the starter manifest's original bytes and
provenance.

Generate the intentionally uncommitted scale artifact with:

```sh
node generate.mjs scale > scale.log
shasum -a 256 -c scale-log.sha256
```

Delete the derived `scale.log` after use. It is deliberately omitted from the
repository because it is about 167,000 human-readable lines and is fully
reconstructible from the committed generator.

Validate the committed action logs with:

```sh
node validate.mjs starter-m1.log starter-m2.log starter-m3.log sample-50.log
```

The validator also accepts a derived log on standard input without writing it:

```sh
node generate.mjs scale | node validate.mjs -
```

## Determinism guarantees

`generate.mjs` uses mulberry32 with seed `20260808`. Every command begins from
that seed and from timestamp `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`; action timestamps advance
by exactly one second. The generator has no wall-clock or ambient-randomness
input. Log timestamps are documentary: replay sequence and server arrival time
remain authoritative.

The PNG generator is a dependency-free bitmap encoder with a bundled 5×7
glyph set. The video generator gives `ffmpeg` fixed synthetic inputs, duration,
codec settings, metadata stripping, and single-threaded x264 settings. Media
contains no captured user data.

The two invariant manifests record generator version/source hash and content
hashes for their adjacent generated logs. The combined manifest pins the scale
log's SHA-256, 167,157-action count, 167,159-line count, and checkpoint prefix
hashes. Regenerating twice on the same toolchain must produce the same bytes;
the checked scale SHA-256 is the cross-run authority.

## Committed versus derived

Committed: schema and documentation, personas, configs, generator and
validator, starter logs, the 50-action sample, both manifests,
`scale-log.sha256`, all media, the media generator, and `VERSION`.

Derived and not committed: `scale.log` and any replay-adapter/backend state
created from it.

content.content:
====M1====
m1-a01 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Sign up as a new user with email + password (password >= 8 chars) succeeds.
m1-a02 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   After signup the app lands in the authenticated state.
m1-a03 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Signing up with a duplicate handle is rejected with a visible error.
m1-a04 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Signing up with a duplicate email is rejected with a visible error.
m1-a05 [choreo] scope=all tags=["app-restart"]
   Kill and relaunch the app; the session persists (still signed in).
   note: App kill/relaunch is client-lifecycle behavior driven by the harness choreography script, not the scripted suite.
m1-a06 [choreo] scope=all tags=["app-restart"]
   Log out, relaunch: the app is signed out.
m1-a07 [grader] scope=full-only tags=["api"]
   After logout the old session token no longer works against the backend (server-side revocation, verified via the API).
   note: The brief marks this API sub-assertion run-scope-conditional: [grader] via the API on full runs only.
m1-a08 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Editing display name and bio persists (updated values shown on own profile).
m1-a09 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Display-name and bio edits are visible on the other client without manual refresh.
m1-a10 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Uploading a fixture avatar succeeds.
m1-a11 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   The uploaded avatar renders on the profile (avatars beside posts and messages are asserted at M2/M3, where those surfaces exist).
m1-a12 [grader] scope=all tags=["source-inspection"]
   Source inspection: passwords are stored via built-in auth or a named adaptive KDF (argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt at standard published parameters); a managed auth provider qualifies by its documentation, with the grader verifying the lane uses the documented provider path, not provider internals.
m1-a13 [grader] scope=all tags=["source-inspection"]
   No plaintext or reversible password storage in server persistence, client bundles, or logs (the fixture pack's credential files are a declared test-fixture exception - they live outside the app).
====M2====
m2-a01 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Create a text post.
m2-a02 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Create an image post with 2 fixture images.
m2-a03 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Create a video post.
m2-a04 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   All three created posts render in the Global feed on the other client without manual refresh.
m2-a05 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client"]
   Feed items render with the author's avatar and display name.
m2-a06 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Bob follows Alice; Alice's posts appear in Bob's Following feed.
m2-a07 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Alice's follower count updates live when Bob follows her.
m2-a08 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   After Bob unfollows, on next feed load Alice's posts (including older ones) no longer appear in his Following feed.
m2-a09 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   After the unfollow, Alice's posts remain visible in the Global feed (unfollow is projection-scoped, not content revocation).
m2-a10 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   A post from a user Bob doesn't follow appears in his Global feed.
m2-a11 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   That same post is absent from Bob's Following feed.
m2-a12 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   An http(s) URL in a text post renders as tappable text opening the system browser.
m2-a13 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   No preview card renders for the URL (no unfurling).
m2-a14 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Like from client B; the like count updates live on client A.
m2-a15 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Unlike works: the like is cleared and the count decrements (idempotent set-state toggle).
m2-a16 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Repost from client B; feeds show the repost attributed 'reposted by {display name}'.
m2-a17 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Reposting again removes the repost (toggle).
m2-a18 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   A repost by a followed user surfaces the original author's post in the Following feed.
m2-a19 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Reply to a post; the parent's reply count increments live.
m2-a20 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   The thread screen shows the parent and its direct replies in chronological order.
m2-a21 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   The reply is absent from both feeds (replies appear only on thread screens).
m2-a22 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   With >20 seeded posts, scrolling loads the next page (20 per page) in the Following tab.
m2-a23 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   With >20 seeded posts, scrolling loads the next page in the Global tab.
m2-a24 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Feed pagination produces no duplicates and no gaps across pages in either tab.
m2-a25 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   With no explicit self-follow edge, Bob's own original posts remain in his Following feed, including when he follows no other accounts.
m2-a26 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   With no explicit self-follow edge, Bob's own reposts remain in his Following feed.
m2-a27 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Implicit self-follow feed membership does not change Bob's follower or following counts.
====M3====
m3-a01 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Alice DMs Bob and Bob replies; both clients see the messages live.
m3-a02 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client"]
   DM messages render with sender avatars.
m3-a03 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Starting the 'same' DM again reuses the existing channel (at most one DM channel per user pair).
m3-a04 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Create a group with Alice, Bob, and Carol.
m3-a05 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   A second group with the same three members coexists as a distinct group.
m3-a06 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Bob types; Alice sees the '…' typing indicator within 2 s.
m3-a07 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   The typing indicator expires within 5 s of Bob's last keystroke.
m3-a08 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client","timing-sensitive"]
   Receipt ticks transition sent -> delivered -> read, monotonically, as Bob's client fetches and then opens the conversation.
m3-a09 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client"]
   The group aggregate indicator shows a state only when every member of the message's recipient set (membership at send time) has reached it - it waits for the slowest member.
m3-a10 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   A quoted reply renders the quoted excerpt in its bubble.
m3-a11 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   Tapping the quoted excerpt scrolls/jumps to the original message.
   note: Single-client UI interaction: suite-covered (web automation), not two-client choreography.
m3-a12 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client"]
   Admin removes Carol; she immediately stops receiving new messages.
m3-a13 [choreo] scope=all tags=["two-client"]
   The removed member still sees her local copy of pre-removal history.
   note: Client-local retention observed on the removed member's client.
m3-a14 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   A non-admin cannot remove members.
m3-a15 [suite-required] scope=all tags=[]
   The seed is idempotent: a second run produces no duplicates - judged per installed segment, covering every starter-log segment installed so far (each milestone's suite re-runs this).

# Social-messenger choreography receipts

Version `0.3.3-m8` writes newline-delimited JSON to `receipts.jsonl`. The same
objects are written to stdout with the literal prefix `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` so
an outer run harness can separate proof records from ordinary process output.
Each line validates independently against `receipts.schema.json`.

## Assertion receipts

Every browser check emits one `type: "assertion"` object. Its stable identity
is `(segment, assertion)`. The required proof fields are:

- `segment`: one of `m1` through `m6`, or `m8`.
- `assertion`: the stable choreography assertion name.
- `implemented`: whether this harness version actually attempted the check.
- `required`: whether leaving this assertion unimplemented blocks the segment.
- `status`: `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped`.
- `pass`: boolean for an attempted check and `null` for an explicit skip.
- `timings`: every attempt, including errors and all three timing attempts.
- `bestOf`: `1` for ordinary checks and `3` for timing-sensitive checks.

Every timing has both `durationMs` (complete check-attempt wall) and
`settlementWaitMs` (the union of actual locator, predicate, and page-event
wait intervals during that attempt). The latter excludes setup, browser
actions, and computation, and therefore never exceeds `durationMs`. D0.6
choreography wait observations are derived from `settlementWaitMs`, not from
whole-attempt duration. The suite producer records its own settlement waits in
the production lane-controller stream; choreography does not claim them.

An unsupported check is not omitted and never passes. It has
`implemented:false`, `status:"skipped"`, `pass:null`, an empty `timings` array,
and a non-empty `details.reason`. A required skip blocks choreography green; an
optional skip remains visible without being reported as a failed attempt.

For `bestOf:3`, the harness always runs all three attempts. The assertion passes
when at least one attempt passes, and `details.selectedAttempt` identifies the
fastest passing attempt by total `durationMs`; all attempts remain in the
receipt. Metric-specific durations such as `visibleMs` and `expiresMs` remain
under each attempt's `metrics` object. This is best-of-three flake control, not
permission to discard measurements.

For M3's `quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` assertion, each attempt's existing
`timing.note` records the `sm-convo-quote-preview` jump selector.

## Segment summaries and milestone green

After the assertion lines, each selected milestone emits one
`type: "segment-summary"` object. This is the per-segment object consumed by the
outer run harness:

```json
{
  "type": "segment-summary",
  "segment": "m3",
  "assertion": "__segment__",
  "implemented": false,
  "required": true,
  "status": "failed",
  "pass": false,
  "timings": [
    {
      "attempt": 1,
      "pass": false,
      "startedAt": null,
      "durationMs": 18234.5,
      "settlementWaitMs": 18001.2,
      "metrics": {}
    }
  ],
  "bestOf": 1,
  "assertions": {
    "total": 3,
    "required": 3,
    "implemented": 2,
    "passed": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skipped": 1,
    "notImplemented": 1,
    "requiredUnimplemented": 1
  },
  "suite": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m3.json" },
  "choreography": {
    "browserPass": false,
    "requiredExternal": [],
    "externalPass": true,
    "supplementalExternal": [],
    "pass": false
  },
  "green": false,
  "nonGreenCause": "required-unimplemented"
}
```

The normative aggregation is:

1. `browserPass` is true only when every implemented assertion passes and no
   required assertion remains unimplemented. Optional skips therefore stay
   explicit without becoming silent failed attempts.
2. `externalPass` is true when every external leg required for web green passes.
   In `0.3.3-m8` there are no such legs. M6's `ios-simulator-m6` and M8's
   `ios-simulator-m8` statuses are recorded in their matching summaries under
   `supplementalExternal` with `requiredForGreen:false`; they are distinct
   native/O4 artifacts governed by `simulator.md`.
3. `choreography.pass` (and the summary's top-level `pass`) is
   `browserPass && externalPass === true`.
4. `green` is true only when `suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true`.
   Version `0.3.3-m8` refuses missing or partial suite-status linkage before
   creating receipts or starting a browser, so emitted `suite.pass` is always
   boolean.
5. `nonGreenCause` is the closed recording convention for a non-green
   segment. It is optional on the schema (default `null` when omitted) so
   existing `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain valid; emitters since `0.3.1-m8`
   always write it. Allowed values:
   - `null` — `green` is true. There is no second green label.
   - `required-unimplemented` — a required assertion was skipped.
   - `choreography-failed` — an implemented assertion failed.
   - `suite-failed` — suite evidence is `pass:false`.
   - `instrument` — non-green for an instrument defect other than missing
     suite linkage, which `0.3.3-m8` refuses before startup.

   Lanes MUST copy `nonGreenCause` from this summary into the run record.
   Do not invent labels such as "functionally green". `green` stays a
   boolean; `capability-failure` remains the brief's cap-exhausted
   milestone status, not a synonym for instrument-caused non-green.

The required suite-status input is an object keyed by milestone. Every selected
milestone must be present:

```json
{
  "m1": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m1.json" },
  "m2": { "pass": false, "receipt": "acceptance/m2.json" },
  "m8": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m8.json" }
}
```

The path is relative to the suite-status file. The choreography does not
interpret or bless the builder's suite semantics, but it does stat and digest
the actual file before startup. The segment summary retains that SHA-256; the
meter re-stats and re-digests the same file at record-write time. A missing or
changed passing receipt refuses rather than becoming green. Coverage-manifest
validation belongs to the outer run harness described by the benchmark brief.

## Compatibility

Consumers must reject an unknown major receipt version and validate with the
schema matching the declared version; unknown fields are rejected. Stable
`(segment, assertion)` names must not be silently repurposed;
changed semantics require a version bump. `nonGreenCause` is an optional
additive field introduced on `0.3.1-m8` segment summaries (default `null`
when omitted); it did not bump the receipt version. `0.3.2-m8` IS a semantic
bump: it removes the legacy `sm-convo-quote` jump fallback, so an M3
`quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` receipt at `0.3.2-m8` proves preview-only
selection, while a `0.3.1-m8` receipt may have recorded the reply-bubble-
scoped fallback.

`0.3.3-m8` keeps `0.3.2-m8` selector semantics and makes suite-status linkage
startup-refusing. It coordinates the additive LLP 0295 D0.6 run-record
observability fields without changing `extensionVersion: 2`; the W2 token
meter now joins typed, hash-verified observation sidecars beside its native
usage stream. Its timing records distinguish complete attempt wall from actual
settlement wait. A missing-linkage `0.3.2-m8` receipt remains governed by its
matching schema and may carry `suite.pass:null`; `0.3.3-m8` never emits that
state.

For `bestOf:3`, the harness always runs all three attempts. The assertion passes
when at least one attempt passes, and `details.selectedAttempt` identifies the
fastest passing attempt by total `durationMs`; all attempts remain in the
receipt. Metric-specific durations such as `visibleMs` and `expiresMs` remain
under each attempt's `metrics` object. This is best-of-three flake control, not
permission to discard measurements.

For M3's `quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` assertion, each attempt's existing
`timing.note` records the `sm-convo-quote-preview` jump selector.

## Segment summaries and milestone green

After the assertion lines, each selected milestone emits one
`type: "segment-summary"` object. This is the per-segment object consumed by the
outer run harness:

```json
{
  "type": "segment-summary",
  "segment": "m3",
  "assertion": "__segment__",
  "implemented": false,
  "required": true,
  "status": "failed",
  "pass": false,
  "timings": [
    {
      "attempt": 1,
      "pass": false,
      "startedAt": null,
      "durationMs": 18234.5,
      "settlementWaitMs": 18001.2,
      "metrics": {}
    }
  ],
  "bestOf": 1,
  "assertions": {
    "total": 3,
    "required": 3,
    "implemented": 2,
    "passed": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skipped": 1,
    "notImplemented": 1,
    "requiredUnimplemented": 1
  },
  "suite": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m3.json" },
  "choreography": {
    "browserPass": false,
    "requiredExternal": [],
    "externalPass": true,
    "supplementalExternal": [],
    "pass": false
  },
  "green": false,
  "nonGreenCause": "required-unimplemented"
}
```

The normative aggregation is:

1. `browserPass` is true only when every implemented assertion passes and no
   required assertion remains unimplemented. Optional skips therefore stay
   explicit without becoming silent failed attempts.
2. `externalPass` is true when every external leg required for web green passes.
   In `0.3.3-m8` there are no such legs. M6's `ios-simulator-m6` and M8's
   `ios-simulator-m8` statuses are recorded in their matching summaries under
   `supplementalExternal` with `requiredForGreen:false`; they are distinct
   native/O4 artifacts governed by `simulator.md`.
3. `choreography.pass` (and the summary's top-level `pass`) is
   `browserPass && externalPass === true`.
4. `green` is true only when `suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true`.
   Version `0.3.3-m8` refuses missing or partial suite-status linkage before
   creating receipts or starting a browser, so emitted `suite.pass` is always
   boolean.
5. `nonGreenCause` is the closed recording convention for a non-green
   segment. It is optional on the schema (default `null` when omitted) so
   existing `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain valid; emitters since `0.3.1-m8`
   always write it. Allowed values:
   - `null` — `green` is true. There is no second green label.
   - `required-unimplemented` — a required assertion was skipped.
   - `choreography-failed` — an implemented assertion failed.
   - `suite-failed` — suite evidence is `pass:false`.
   - `instrument` — non-green for an instrument defect other than missing
     suite linkage, which `0.3.3-m8` refuses before startup.

   Lanes MUST copy `nonGreenCause` from this summary into the run record.
   Do not invent labels such as "functionally green". `green` stays a
   boolean; `capability-failure` remains the brief's cap-exhausted
   milestone status, not a synonym for instrument-caused non-green.

The required suite-status input is an object keyed by milestone. Every selected
milestone must be present:

```json
{
  "m1": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m1.json" },
  "m2": { "pass": false, "receipt": "acceptance/m2.json" },
  "m8": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m8.json" }
}
```

The path is relative to the suite-status file. The choreography does not
interpret or bless the builder's suite semantics, but it does stat and digest
the actual file before startup. The segment summary retains that SHA-256; the
meter re-stats and re-digests the same file at record-write time. A missing or
changed passing receipt refuses rather than becoming green. Coverage-manifest
validation belongs to the outer run harness described by the benchmark brief.

## Compatibility

Consumers must reject an unknown major receipt version and validate with the
schema matching the declared version; unknown fields are rejected. Stable
`(segment, assertion)` names must not be silently repurposed;
changed semantics require a version bump. `nonGreenCause` is an optional
additive field introduced on `0.3.1-m8` segment summaries (default `null`
when omitted); it did not bump the receipt version. `0.3.2-m8` IS a semantic
bump: it removes the legacy `sm-convo-quote` jump fallback, so an M3
`quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` receipt at `0.3.2-m8` proves preview-only
selection, while a `0.3.1-m8` receipt may have recorded the reply-bubble-
scoped fallback.

`0.3.3-m8` keeps `0.3.2-m8` selector semantics and makes suite-status linkage
startup-refusing. It coordinates the additive LLP 0295 D0.6 run-record
observability fields without changing `extensionVersion: 2`; the W2 token
meter now joins typed, hash-verified observation sidecars beside its native
usage stream. Its timing records distinguish complete attempt wall from actual
settlement wait. A missing-linkage `0.3.2-m8` receipt remains governed by its
matching schema and may carry `suite.pass:null`; `0.3.3-m8` never emits that
state.

# @snapback-bench/social-ui

Presentational UI kit for the **social-messenger** canonical
benchmark (app name: **Clique**). Version: see [`VERSION`](./VERSION)
(`0.3.1-m8`; the P3 freeze bumps to `1.0.0` and pins hashes in the
brief). Governing design: LLP 0201 D6
(`llp/0201-social-messenger-canonical-benchmark.plan.md`);
coordination pins: `benchmarks/tools/social-messenger/CONTRACT.md`;
product truth: `benchmarks/briefs/social-messenger.md`.

## What this is

React Native + TypeScript components, built against bare RN
primitives, for every pinned Clique screen — so benchmark lanes spend
their wall clock on the backend, not on pixels, and so grader
automation finds identical test IDs in every lane. The kit is a
**symmetric aid** disclosed under LLP 0197 rule 10 and is frozen with
the brief at P3.

Components: `MessageBubble`, `ChatListRow`, `Composer`, `FeedCard`,
`Avatar`, `ProfileForm`, `ReactionPicker`, `TypingIndicator`,
`ReceiptTicks`, `QuotedReply`, `PollCompose`, `PollDisplay`,
`FeedTabs`, `SearchBar`, `ChatSettingsForm`, `AuthForm`,
`InsightsSummary`, `InsightsBarList`, `TrendingRow`, `TrendingEmpty` —
plus the design tokens in `src/tokens.ts` (spacing, radii, type scale,
palette, and the pinned 8 chat accent colors: indigo, teal, coral,
amber, violet, emerald, rose, slate). Screen composition notes:
[`screens.md`](./screens.md). Neutrality posture and the pre-freeze
cross-backend review notes: [`NEUTRALITY.md`](./NEUTRALITY.md).

## What this is not

- **Not a data layer.** No fetching, no subscriptions, no context
  providers, no storage, no navigation. Zero runtime dependencies
  beyond `react` and `react-native` (peer dependencies).
- **Not an app shell.** No screens, routers, or lists — lanes own
  Expo Router wiring, virtualized lists, pagination, and state.
- **Not a validator.** Length caps on inputs are affordances;
  every rule the brief pins (handle uniqueness, edit windows,
  permissions) is enforced by the lane's backend and surfaces here
  through plain props (`errorText`, `canEdit`, `disabled`).

## The no-data-assumptions rule

Prop shapes are deliberately naive — a `messages`-style array of
scalars, an `onSend(text)` callback — and must stay that way. No
cursors, subscription objects, async iterators, promise-returning
callbacks, or client handles may be added, because any of those would
favor one backend architecture over another (reactive vs
fetch-shaped). The full posture, per component, is in
[`NEUTRALITY.md`](./NEUTRALITY.md). Changes to any prop shape are a
kit version change and re-open the neutrality review.

## Usage

Lanes vendor or path-import the kit and wire data around it:

```tsx
import { Composer, MessageBubble, TypingIndicator } from '@snapback-bench/social-ui';

// Data from wherever the lane's backend puts it — live query, fetch,
// offline store. The kit only sees plain values.
<MessageBubble
  isMine={false}
  senderName="Bob"
  showSender
  text="on my way"
  timestamp="12:04"
  reactions={[{ emoji: '👍', count: 2, mine: true }]}
  onPressReactionChip={(emoji) => clearOrSetReaction(emoji)}
/>
<TypingIndicator visible={someoneTyping} names={typingNames} />
<Composer
  variant="message"
  value={draft}
  onChangeText={setDraft}
  onSend={(text) => sendMessage(text)}
/>
```

Every interactive/observable kit element carries its exact component-level
contract testID from `CONTRACT.md` (scheme `sm-<area>-<element>`). Lane shells
own the route- and message-action IDs that require application state or
navigation. Choreography consumes only the shared contract set.

## Tests

```
cd benchmarks/tools/social-messenger/ui
npm install
npm test
```

The suite checks contract-ID defaults and typechecks the package. `react`,
`react-native`, and `@types/react` are devDependencies for typechecking only;
at runtime they are peers supplied by the lane's app.

## Versioning

`VERSION`, `package.json`, and the brief's pinned kit version move together.
`0.3.1-m8` migrates the pressable quoted excerpt to
`sm-convo-quote-preview`, reserving `sm-convo-quote` for the lane-owned
per-message Reply action. `0.3.0-m8` added the M8 Insights and Trending
surfaces; `0.2.0-p2` added the accessible state consumed by the hardened
choreography. The P3 freeze bumps to `1.0.0` after the cross-backend neutrality review and
pilot shakedown, and the frozen hash is recorded in the brief. Post-freeze
changes require a version bump and re-disclosure per LLP 0197.
=== VERSION ===
0.3.1-m8
=== package.json ===
{
  "name": "@snapback-bench/social-ui",
  "version": "0.3.1-m8",
  "private": true,
  "description": "Purely presentational UI kit for the social-messenger (Clique) benchmark. LLP 0201 D6.",
  "main": "index.ts",
  "types": "index.ts",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test test/*.test.mjs && npm run typecheck",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p ."
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": ">=18",
    "react-native": ">=0.74"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/react": "~19.2.0",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.2",
    "typescript": "^5.5.0"
  }
}

# Clique — screen wireframes (kit composition notes)

Wireframe notes for the brief's pinned screens
(`benchmarks/briefs/social-messenger.md`, "Screens (pinned)"). Each
entry lists the kit components that compose the screen, an ASCII
layout sketch, and the contract testIDs that appear
(`benchmarks/tools/social-messenger/CONTRACT.md`). The kit is purely
presentational (LLP 0201 D6): lanes wire all data, navigation,
scrolling/virtualized lists, and screen chrome (headers, back
buttons, tab bars). Sketches show intent, not pixels.

Legend: `[...]` interactive element · `#id` = contract testID on that
element · `(#id)` = extra kit testID (non-contract, stable).

---

## 1. Auth (sign up / sign in)

Components: **AuthForm**

```
+--------------------------------------+
|                                      |
|               Clique                 |
|                                      |
|  [ email                ] #sm-auth-email
|  [ password             ] #sm-auth-password
|  ( error text, if any )   (#sm-auth-error)
|  [       Sign up        ] #sm-auth-submit
|   Already have an account? Sign in   |  (#sm-auth-toggle)
+--------------------------------------+
```

Contract IDs: `sm-auth-email`, `sm-auth-password`, `sm-auth-submit`.

## 2. Feed (Following / Global / Trending tabs)

Components: **FeedTabs**, **FeedCard** (per post), **Avatar** (inside
FeedCard). The lane provides the scrolling list, 20-per-page infinite
scroll, and tab state. The M8 Trending composition is detailed in section 14.

```
+--------------------------------------+
| [ Following ] [ Global ] [ Trending ]| #sm-feed-tab-following / #sm-feed-tab-global / #sm-feed-tab-trending
|=====────────      ───────   ────────  |
| +----------------------------------+ |
| | (o) Alice @alice · 2h            | | #sm-feed-item (card)
| |     Coffee time https://…        | |
| |     [img][img]                   | |
| |  [◗ 3]     [↻ 1]     [♡ 12]      | | #sm-post-reply / #sm-post-repost / #sm-post-like
| +----------------------------------+ |
| | ↻ Reposted by Bob                | | (#sm-feed-repost-attribution)
| | (o) Carol @carol · 5h  …         | | #sm-feed-item
| +----------------------------------+ |
+--------------------------------------+
```

Contract IDs: `sm-feed-tab-following`, `sm-feed-tab-global`,
`sm-feed-tab-trending`,
`sm-feed-item`, `sm-post-like`, `sm-post-repost`, `sm-post-reply`.

## 3. Post thread

Components: **FeedCard** (parent, then each direct reply,
chronological). The lane supplies the screen and ordering.

```
+--------------------------------------+
| < Thread                             |  (lane chrome)
| +----------------------------------+ |
| | (o) Alice — parent post          | | #sm-feed-item
| |  [◗ 2] [↻] [♡]                   | | #sm-post-reply / -repost / -like
| +----------------------------------+ |
| |  (o) Bob — reply 1               | | #sm-feed-item
| |  (o) Carol — reply 2             | | #sm-feed-item
| +----------------------------------+ |
+--------------------------------------+
```

Contract IDs: `sm-feed-item`, `sm-post-like`, `sm-post-repost`,
`sm-post-reply` (same FeedCard set; replies are posts).

## 4. Compose post

Components: **Composer** (`variant="post"`). Attachment picking (1–4
fixture images or exactly one video, per brief M2) is lane logic; the
kit previews whatever `attachments` it is handed.

```
+--------------------------------------+
| < Cancel                             |  (lane chrome)
|  [thumb][thumb]  ✕                   |  (#sm-compose-attachment-remove)
|  [＋] [ What's happening?      ][Post]| (#sm-compose-attach) #sm-compose-input #sm-compose-submit
+--------------------------------------+
```

Contract IDs: `sm-compose-input`, `sm-compose-submit`.

## 5. Own profile (view + edit)

Components: **ProfileForm** (`mode="view-own"` then `mode="edit"`),
**Avatar**, **FeedCard** for the user's posts below (lane list).

```
View:                                Edit:
+---------------------------+       +---------------------------+
| (O)          [Edit profile]|#sm-profile-edit | (O) Change photo (#sm-profile-avatar)
| Alice                     |       | Display name [        ]   | (#sm-profile-field-displayname)
| @alice                    |       | Handle       [        ]   | (#sm-profile-field-handle)
| bio…  link                |       | Bio          [        ]   | (#sm-profile-field-bio)
| 12 Followers · 34 Following|      | Location     [        ]   | (#sm-profile-field-location)
| (#sm-profile-follower-count|      | Link         [        ]   | (#sm-profile-field-link)
|  #sm-profile-following-count)     | [        Save         ]   | #sm-profile-save
| ── posts (FeedCard list) ──|      +---------------------------+
+---------------------------+
```

Contract IDs: `sm-profile-edit`, `sm-profile-save` (+ FeedCard IDs in
the posts list).

## 6. Other-user profile

Components: **ProfileForm** (`mode="view-other"`), **Avatar**,
**FeedCard** list below.

```
+--------------------------------------+
| (O)                  [ Follow ]      | #sm-profile-follow (toggle)

# Social-messenger action-log grammar

Version: `0.1.0-p1`

This file freezes the human-readable grammar for the Clique fixture pack. The
machine-readable authority is [`action-schema.json`](./action-schema.json). A
replay adapter must implement every verb below; silently skipping a recognized
verb is nonconforming.

## Replay and settling

Each action line has this shape:

```text
<ISO8601> <actor> <verb> <args...>
```

The timestamp is an RFC 3339 UTC instant with whole-second precision, such as
`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. It is documentary. Replay order and the backend's server
arrival time determine ordering; adapters must not backdate records from the
fixture timestamp.

The adapter must submit one action and wait for an authoritative receipt before
it can proceed. Only authoritative success permits the next action; a terminal
failure ends replay and is reported. “Settled” means the app's own auth and
mutation path has accepted the write, not merely that a request was queued
locally. A checkpoint is reached only after the action immediately before its
marker has settled. Push emission is disabled for scale replay, while receipts
and feed behavior remain enabled.

The two non-action marker lines are exactly:

```text
# checkpoint 10%
# checkpoint 50%
```

On a marker, pause, verify the matching checkpoint sub-manifest, run the probe
set, and then continue. Blank lines are forbidden.

## Lexical rules

Arguments are separated by one or more ASCII spaces or tabs. IDs, enums, email
addresses, URLs, media paths, and mutation IDs are bare tokens. Free text,
passwords, captions, and emoji are JSON string literals in double quotes;
normal JSON escapes apply. There is no shell interpolation. A media list is one
bare comma-separated token with one to four PNG paths and no spaces.

Actors are fixture user IDs. A create verb's explicit ID is a client-generated,
stable idempotency key as well as the desired entity ID. `follow`, `like`,
`repost`, and `react` are set-state intents, never toggles. Their mutation IDs
make retry behavior observable and idempotent.

## Frozen verbs

### `register`

```text
register <email> "<password>"
```

The actor is the new user ID. Registration uses the application's real signup
path.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:00Z alice register alice@example.com "Alice!Clique2026"
```

### `profile-set`

```text
profile-set "<displayName>" <handle> "<bio>" "<location>" <link> <avatarPng>
```

This is a complete replacement of the actor's five textual profile fields and
avatar reference.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:01Z alice profile-set "Alice Alvarez" alice "Coffee and cameras." "Oakland, CA" https://example.com/alice media/avatar-alice.png
```

### `follow`

```text
follow <targetUserId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the edge exists; `clear` ensures it does not.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:02Z alice follow bob set mut-follow-alice-bob
```

### `post`

```text
post <postId> text "<text>"
post <postId> images "<text>" <pngPath[,pngPath...]>
post <postId> video "<text>" <mp4Path>
```

The text body may be `""`. Images accept one to four fixture PNGs. Video
accepts exactly `media/vid-01.mp4`. Images and video never mix.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:03Z alice post sp0001 text "Coffee time https://example.com/cafe"
2026-01-01T00:00:04Z bob post sp0002 images "Two views" media/img-01.png,media/img-02.png
2026-01-01T00:00:05Z carol post sp0003 video "Five quiet seconds" media/vid-01.mp4
```

### `like`

```text
like <postId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the actor likes the post; `clear` ensures they do not.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:06Z bob like sp0001 set mut-like-bob-sp0001
```

### `repost`

```text
repost <postId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the actor's repost exists; `clear` removes that actor's repost.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:07Z carol repost sp0001 set mut-repost-carol-sp0001
```

### `reply`

```text
reply <replyId> <parentPostId> "<text>"
```

A reply is a post entity that references its direct parent. Replies do not
enter either feed.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:08Z bob reply sr0001 sp0001 "Save me a cup."
```

### `dm-create`

```text
dm-create <conversationId> <otherUserId>
```

The actor is the first participant. Replaying a DM create for an existing pair
must resolve to that pair's single DM rather than create a duplicate.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:09Z alice dm-create d-alice-bob bob
```

### `group-create`

```text
group-create <conversationId> <secondMemberUserId> "<name>" "<description>"
```

The actor is the creator/admin and first member. The named second member makes
the group valid at creation. Use `""` for no description.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:10Z alice group-create g-starter bob "Weekend Plans" "Coffee and a walk."
```

### `member-add`

```text
member-add <conversationId> <memberUserId> <mutationId>
```

The actor must be a group admin. Replay ensures the membership exists.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:11Z alice member-add g-starter carol mut-member-g-starter-carol
```

### `send`

```text
send <messageId> <conversationId> "<text>"
send <messageId> <conversationId> "<text>" quote=<messageId>
```

The optional `quote=` token points at an earlier message in the same
conversation. It is a quoted reply, not a thread.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:12Z alice send sm0001 d-alice-bob "Are you nearby?"
2026-01-01T00:00:13Z bob send sm0002 d-alice-bob "Five minutes away." quote=sm0001
```

### `send-media`

```text
send-media <messageId> <conversationId> <image|video> <mediaPath> "<caption>" <normal|view-once>
```

Images use fixture PNGs; video uses the fixture MP4. Only images may be
`view-once`. Use `""` for no caption.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:14Z alice send-media sm0003 d-alice-bob image media/img-03.png "Found it" normal
2026-01-01T00:00:15Z bob send-media sm0004 d-alice-bob image media/img-04.png "One look" view-once
```

### `react`

```text
react <messageId> "<emoji|none>" <mutationId>
```

Any emoji string sets or replaces the actor's one reaction. The exact quoted
string `"none"` clears it.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:16Z carol react sm0001 "👍" mut-react-carol-sm0001
2026-01-01T00:00:17Z carol react sm0001 "none" mut-react-clear-carol-sm0001
```

## Adapter conformance

`sample-50.log` contains exactly 50 actions and covers every verb and every
post variant, both `send` forms, both media kinds, view-once, and set/clear
intents. Syntax validation is necessary but not sufficient: M6 conformance
requires replay through the app's own paths with a settle receipt for each
action and the resulting state matching those intents.

make retry behavior observable and idempotent.

## Frozen verbs

### `register`

```text
register <email> "<password>"
```

The actor is the new user ID. Registration uses the application's real signup
path.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:00Z alice register alice@example.com "Alice!Clique2026"
```

### `profile-set`

```text
profile-set "<displayName>" <handle> "<bio>" "<location>" <link> <avatarPng>
```

This is a complete replacement of the actor's five textual profile fields and
avatar reference.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:01Z alice profile-set "Alice Alvarez" alice "Coffee and cameras." "Oakland, CA" https://example.com/alice media/avatar-alice.png
```

### `follow`

```text
follow <targetUserId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the edge exists; `clear` ensures it does not.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:02Z alice follow bob set mut-follow-alice-bob
```

### `post`

```text
post <postId> text "<text>"
post <postId> images "<text>" <pngPath[,pngPath...]>
post <postId> video "<text>" <mp4Path>
```

The text body may be `""`. Images accept one to four fixture PNGs. Video
accepts exactly `media/vid-01.mp4`. Images and video never mix.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:03Z alice post sp0001 text "Coffee time https://example.com/cafe"
2026-01-01T00:00:04Z bob post sp0002 images "Two views" media/img-01.png,media/img-02.png
2026-01-01T00:00:05Z carol post sp0003 video "Five quiet seconds" media/vid-01.mp4
```

### `like`

```text
like <postId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the actor likes the post; `clear` ensures they do not.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:06Z bob like sp0001 set mut-like-bob-sp0001
```

### `repost`

```text
repost <postId> <set|clear> <mutationId>
```

`set` ensures the actor's repost exists; `clear` removes that actor's repost.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:07Z carol repost sp0001 set mut-repost-carol-sp0001
```

### `reply`

```text
reply <replyId> <parentPostId> "<text>"
```

A reply is a post entity that references its direct parent. Replies do not
enter either feed.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:08Z bob reply sr0001 sp0001 "Save me a cup."
```

### `dm-create`

```text
dm-create <conversationId> <otherUserId>
```

The actor is the first participant. Replaying a DM create for an existing pair
must resolve to that pair's single DM rather than create a duplicate.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:09Z alice dm-create d-alice-bob bob
```

### `group-create`

```text
group-create <conversationId> <secondMemberUserId> "<name>" "<description>"
```

The actor is the creator/admin and first member. The named second member makes
the group valid at creation. Use `""` for no description.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:10Z alice group-create g-starter bob "Weekend Plans" "Coffee and a walk."
```

### `member-add`

```text
member-add <conversationId> <memberUserId> <mutationId>
```

The actor must be a group admin. Replay ensures the membership exists.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:11Z alice member-add g-starter carol mut-member-g-starter-carol
```

### `send`

```text
send <messageId> <conversationId> "<text>"
send <messageId> <conversationId> "<text>" quote=<messageId>
```

The optional `quote=` token points at an earlier message in the same
conversation. It is a quoted reply, not a thread.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:12Z alice send sm0001 d-alice-bob "Are you nearby?"
2026-01-01T00:00:13Z bob send sm0002 d-alice-bob "Five minutes away." quote=sm0001
```

### `send-media`

```text
send-media <messageId> <conversationId> <image|video> <mediaPath> "<caption>" <normal|view-once>
```

Images use fixture PNGs; video uses the fixture MP4. Only images may be
`view-once`. Use `""` for no caption.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:14Z alice send-media sm0003 d-alice-bob image media/img-03.png "Found it" normal
2026-01-01T00:00:15Z bob send-media sm0004 d-alice-bob image media/img-04.png "One look" view-once
```

### `react`

```text
react <messageId> "<emoji|none>" <mutationId>
```

Any emoji string sets or replaces the actor's one reaction. The exact quoted
string `"none"` clears it.

```text
2026-01-01T00:00:16Z carol react sm0001 "👍" mut-react-carol-sm0001
2026-01-01T00:00:17Z carol react sm0001 "none" mut-react-clear-carol-sm0001
```

## Adapter conformance

`sample-50.log` contains exactly 50 actions and covers every verb and every
post variant, both `send` forms, both media kinds, view-once, and set/clear
intents. Syntax validation is necessary but not sufficient: M6 conformance
requires replay through the app's own paths with a settle receipt for each
action and the resulting state matching those intents.

This packet is the whole required first read for this app (LLP 0259
Rung A). Open the edit targets below and work; open one further Guide page
only via `snapback guide <query>` or on a trigger — the brief is outside
this packet, a structured `SNAPBACK_*` refusal, or a failed `prove`.

## The loop

Edit `snapback/schema.mjs` / `snapback/functions.mjs` / `snapback/seed.json`
→ `bun run generate` → `bun run dev` (supervises the Expo client; it never
launches a device or simulator — Expo Go, a dev client, or
`expo run:ios|android` is your job) → `bun run prove`.

Before extending or ejecting the proof runner, read
`node_modules/@expo/snapback-acceptance/README.md`; it is the supported
compatibility and ownership contract.

<!-- script-glossary:begin -->
## Script glossary

`bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative
aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof).
`npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging).
`bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence.
`bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt,
never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only.
Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command.
<!-- script-glossary:end -->

The native carrier owns simulator boot, drive, and screenshots. Self-started
Metro must not inherit `CI=1` (it disables watching); prefer `bun run dev`.

## Edit targets (work files — listed, not charged to the first read)

- `snapback/schema.mjs` — sessions auth; user/conversation/membership/message/
  reaction tables; ephemeral `typing`.
- `snapback/functions.mjs` — inbox and thread live queries, `sendText` /
  `sendReply` / `react` mutations, and the bound `send` command.
- `snapback/seed.json` — seeded demo personas and conversations.
- `App.tsx` — generated `app` → `SnapbackExpoProvider`; native retained files;
  password entry via `useSnapbackCurrentPrincipal` / `useSnapbackAuth`.
- `src/screens/inbox-screen.tsx` / `src/screens/chat-screen.tsx` — the
  `useSnapbackQuery` inbox and `useSurface` thread (replies, reactions,
  typing, upload) from `@expo/snapback-expo`.
- `acceptance.mjs` + `snapback.verify.config.mjs` — the registered proof.

`snapback/generated/` is codegen-owned: regenerate, commit
`generated/artifacts.json`, never hand-edit outputs.

## Posture

- **Auth: sessions mode, guest-first plus ordinary password entry.** The
  app reaches anonymous `ready`; recovery codes surface once after signup.
  Supervised dev may provide a guest session for sends and image upload.
- **Custody: `volatile-explicit`.** Native durable custody is still pending
  Phase 2, so this disposable chat template says memory custody explicitly;
  it does not claim durable native custody or silently weaken a durable
  policy. Move to `durable-required` only after the native platform row ships.
- **Security caveat — client-supplied `senderId` is a demo convenience,
  never a boundary.** The seeded **TEST PERSONA** control passes the active
  persona's id as `senderId`/`userId` so demos work. In a real app, derive
  the sender from the adopted session on the server (`ctx.auth.userId`),
  drop the argument, and keep personas display-only.

1. Declare each function's `auth` explicitly in sessions mode: omitting it
   gets legacy `optional-user` widening plus the

2. Inline args objects churn `useSnapbackQuery` — the subscription keys on
   args identity; hoist or memoize.
3. Structured stored fields (`v.array(...)`, `v.object({...})`) are typed
   but opaque (experimental): interiors are not queryable, and a nested
   `v.principal()` is a snapshot, not membership.
4. A changed seed identity never silently resets data: expect
   `SNAPBACK_SEED_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, then migrate or reset-install.
5. Every `SNAPBACK_*` refusal names its rule and fix: read it, then run
   `snapback guide <CODE>` for the exact entry.

`snapback guide <query>` returns exact symbols, diagnostic codes, and page
anchors — budgeted lookups do not count as extra pages. The

[surfaces](/_snapback/guide/clients/surfaces.md),
[sessions and principals](/_snapback/guide/auth/sessions-and-principals.md),
[assets](/_snapback/guide/backend/assets.md),
[ephemeral state](/_snapback/guide/realtime/ephemeral-state.md).

and outside this template. If a brief selects it, read the
[Familiar handler dialect](/_snapback/guide/backend/familiar-profile.md) before editing.
<!-- /llp0259:stop-fence -->
<!-- start-packet:end -->

## Operate it

`snapback mcp` serves read-only Guide resources; `snapback mcp-control` adds
typed control tools with local admin authority. Preview setup with
`snapback agent setup --print <client> --server mcp-control`. With the dev
server running this packet is served at
`http://127.0.0.1:4287/_snapback/guide/start/expo-chat.md` (replace the
origin if startup selected another port); `snapback guide <query>` is the
budgeted lookup channel.

`.claude/skills/snapback-authoring/SKILL.md` (mirrored under `.agents/`,
`.cursor/`, and `.opencode/`); it repeats this packet-first contract.

Need an exact exported signature? Start with the build-bound [generated API reference](./reference/index.md), or run `snapback guide ` for a budgeted symbol lookup. For a stable `SNAPBACK_*` failure, use the generated [diagnostic code registry](./reference/diagnostics.md), or pass the code to the same command for exact lookup before prose search. **Audience:** agents (primarily) and humans (secondarily) building on Snapback. In a checkout, read this corpus directly. Outside a checkout, a running Snapback server exposes the same build-bound corpus at `GET /_snapback/guide` and individual paths below that prefix. The first read is deliberately small (LLP 0259): a template's [start packet](./start/index.md), or [Snapback in one screen](./start/mental-model.md) when no template is selected — then escalate one page at a time. The [capability index](./capabilities.md) and [surface map](./surface-map.md) are budgeted registries for lookup, not linear first reads. Generated `guide-flat.
.generated.md` files provide a per-section bulk tier. The complete bulk projection remains at `GET /_snapback/guide/flat.md`, but is about 2.5 MiB and growing. Those responses carry `x-snapback-guide-content-sha256` and `x-snapback-server-build-commit`, so a consumer can refuse to combine cached guide bytes with a different server build. `GET /llms.txt` at the served root provides a convention-standard index in that recommended order, with approximate sizes, and lists the whole-corpus projection last as an explicit bulk fallback. The same local server serves `GET /_snapback/guide/http.routes.v1.json`, a generated build-bound join from the installed route registry to committed input/output schema references; a `null` schema reference means no route-specific schema is committed, not an unconstrained body. Building Snapback itself is a different job — that's `AGENTS.md` and the LLP corpus, not this guide. That served-discovery promise is for local/embedded server profiles. The derived hosted posture deliberately disables `operatorSurface`; on that profile `/llms.txt`, `/_snapback/guide*`, `/_snapback/api/control-catalog`, and host-operation discovery are not claimed. Depending on the target, those URLs may return a fixed empty 404, an asset fallback, or a target-specific refusal; none is evidence of a hosted discovery surface. Use the guide from the pinned checkout or published package when working against that profile; do not infer local discovery routes from a hosted app's root URL. ## Choose the MCP authority Snapback ships two local stdio MCP servers. Keep their different authority postures visible when you configure an agent: | Server | What it exposes | Authority consequence | | --- | --- | --- | | `snapback mcp` | The native Rust binary's resource-only Guide server. It reads the compile-time-embedded Guide corpus and exposes the manifest, per-section flats, the roughly 2.5 MiB whole-corpus bulk flat, and manifest-named pages at stable `snapback-guide://` URIs. Context-limited readers should prefer the `start.*` packet pages or a section; capabilities is a lookup registry. It has no mutation or host-operation tools. | Least authority: safe to wire into any agent, with no additional authority grant. | | `snapback mcp-control` | The explicit JS control-plane server shipped by `@expo/snapback-cli`: typed control tools, the generated app-data catalog, `snapback-controls://catalog` plus per-operation/instance resources, and the native Guide resources. It invokes the co-installed native runtime for both embedded Guide and build-catalog bytes; the npm package carries no second snapshot. If that binary is unavailable, resource listing reports `SNAPBACK_MCP_NATIVE_DOCUMENTATION_UNAVAILABLE` and lists no pretend Guide/catalog resources. | Standing local admin: it authenticates with the auto-minted local admin token, so the wired-in client has admin authority over the local Snapback instance. | The split makes documentation safe by default while keeping a capable operating surface available by explicit choice. `mcp-control` has the same local authority the CLI already exercises, but it is still a real authority grant that a cold agent must understand before opting in; configuring it does not grant hosted or remote authority, and no credential is copied into MCP configuration. Generate the project-scoped configuration instead of guessing client syntax: ```sh snapback agent setup --print codex snapback agent setup --print claude --server mcp snapback agent setup --install cursor --server mcp-control ``` `--print` supports `codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, and `generic`; without `--server` it prints both entries. Codex uses `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project, Claude uses `.mcp.json`, and Cursor uses `.cursor/mcp.json`. Installation and exact uninstall require an explicit `--server mcp|mcp-control`; installation shows the target file, requested server, and authority consequence before it writes, then returns a receipt. For a manual setup, the two commands are simply: ```sh snapback mcp snapback mcp-control ``` A project-scoped JSON client entry has this minimal shape when the installed `@expo/snapback-cli` `snapback` bin is on `PATH` (the setup command emits the resolved local executable paths instead): ```json fragment reason="manual MCP client configuration; generated executable paths are installation-specific" { "mcpServers": { "snapback-guide": { "command": "snapback", "args": ["mcp"] }, "snapback-control": { "command": "snapback", "args": ["mcp-control"] }

# Sessions and principals

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](./targets.md).

The one idea (LLP 0039): **the server derives who you are; the client never
asserts it.** In sessions mode, `ctx.auth` comes only from a server-minted
session resolved at one invocation gate covering every entry path — HTTP,
WebSocket, everything. Everything this page teaches is witnessed by
`demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs`, which runs in the
local proof.

Auth mode is per-app schema config
(`auth: { mode: 'dev' | 'sessions' }` in `defineSchema` — see
[your first backend](../getting-started/your-first-backend.md)). `dev` mode
is the trusted-local convenience where tests pass `userId:` directly;
`sessions` is the real thing below.

That dev-mode assertion now has a per-boot `sbdev_` custody capability,
separate from sessions, admin tokens, and impersonation. The ready descriptor
names its owner-only sidecar in `devIdentityCapabilityFile`; direct/headless
clients and the demo kit read it, managed Vite stamps it behind the same-origin
relay, external dev hosts receive `SNAPBACK_DEV_IDENTITY_FILE`, and supervised
native Expo redeems a one-shot launch nonce. Stage 1 verifies any capability
that is presented but still accepts an absent one with a single server warning
per boot. Missing capability becomes a refusal only at LLP 0262's enforce
stage, after every supported carrier has an acceptance witness; none of this
adds a second gate to admin-token-gated `function.run` or `auth.mintSession`.

## Choose each function's auth requirement

Every user-authored function in a sessions-mode app should explicitly set one
of these requirements:

| `auth` value | Invocation rule |
| --- | --- |
| `'public'` | Anonymous and user-bearing callers are admitted after any presented credential is validated. This declaration does not by itself prove the function is authority-independent. |
| `'optional-user'` | Anonymous and user-bearing callers are admitted, and the handler may deliberately vary behavior when a resolved user exists. |
| `'authenticated'` | Snapback refuses the invocation before the handler runs unless authority contains a resolved user. |

During the compatibility warning phase, omission still emits the legacy
effective requirement `optional-user`, but codegen reports one
`SNAPBACK_AUTH_REQUIREMENT_IMPLICIT` warning per omitted sessions function.
Fix it by adding the intended `auth: 'public'`, `auth: 'optional-user'`, or
`auth: 'authenticated'` field to the function definition; do not treat the
legacy value as an authored choice. Dev-mode functions retain omission as a
trusted-local compatibility convenience and do not produce this warning.

An `authenticated` action cannot be a cron target because scheduled system
authority has no resolved user. Choosing `public` or `optional-user` makes the
cron target compatible with system authority, but does not make it
internal-only or prevent client invocation.

## Provision sessions artifacts explicitly

The legacy `ensureApp({ schema, functions, seed })` request is a settled-dev
compatibility form, not a sessions provisioning authority. Give the client an
admin token and select the closed provision variant:

```js fragment reason="generated manifests and seed are app inputs"
const client = new SnapbackClient(baseUrl, { adminToken });
await client.ensureApp({
  intent: 'provision',
  requestedMode: 'sessions',
  schema,
  functions,
  seed,
});
```

This remains `AdminWrite` and non-production-profile gated before hash
comparison or effects. Staging a fresh `dev → sessions` deployment closes app
data until restart; provisioning an already-settled sessions deployment is
idempotent but still crosses the same authorization gate. Do not hand-write a
`fetch('/app/ensure', ...)` substitute.

For tests and headless suites there is a one-boot form that skips the
provision-then-restart dance entirely: the server-lifecycle kit accepts
the generated startup artifacts directly, so the process comes up already
settled in sessions mode with the impersonation capability captured for
mailbox reads:

```js fragment reason="paths and artifacts are app inputs"
const server = await startServer({
  startupArtifacts,                 // the generated sessions artifacts
  captureImpersonationCapability: true,
});
```

This is the form the acceptance suites use (`demos/_kit/server-process.mjs`);
prefer it over provision-plus-restart whenever the suite owns the server
process.

## Sign in: email code → session credential

The client requests a code and exchanges it. In tests, the shared `asUser`
helper owns that complete loop, including the admin-gated mailbox read:

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
async function mintSession(server, appId, email, clientStoreId) {
  return asUser(server, appId, email, { clientStoreId });
}
```

The result exposes `client`, the public `session`, `userId`, and an idempotent
`dispose`, plus the coordinator and custody state needed by lower-level tests.
From then on the client carries the session credential; `AuthCoordinator`
(from `@expo/snapback-contract`) owns custody, refresh, and the logout barrier.

For a browser/Vite surface in local development, keep the privileged mailbox
read in a serve-only dev-server relay while the browser performs
`authRequestCode` → relay fetch → `authExchange`. The complete non-React
pattern is [get the sign-in code in local development](../recipes/browser-auth.md#get-the-sign-in-code-in-local-development).

The shipped provider has no production mail adapter yet. For a local native
app whose identity front door lives in trusted server code, use the sanctioned
[external identity-broker seam](./native-apps.md): the broker invokes the
gated non-production session-mint host operation and the first-party client
adopts the resulting bearer with exact protocol offers. Neither path is a
hosted-production auth claim.

## Sign in: email + password

The local target also exposes first-class password credentials. Use
`POST /auth/password/signup` with `{ email, password }` to create a principal,
and `POST /auth/password/signin` with the same closed shape thereafter. Both
return the ordinary credential response used by `/auth/exchange`; the session
provider is `local-password`, including on later refreshes. Signup additionally
returns the one-time recovery codes. Store them at that moment: they cannot be
read back.

Password change is session-authenticated. A password session rotates with
`{ currentPassword, newPassword }`. An email-code session can set its first
password only with `{ currentPassword: null, newPassword, stepUp }`, where the
step-up challenge was minted for that exact email identity and operation. The
server never accepts a caller-supplied `userId`.

Recovery codes are the production-shaped recovery path. Send `{ email, code }`
to `POST /auth/recovery/consume`; success consumes that code, revokes the old
session family, mints a local-password session, and returns a replacement code
set exactly once. A local-password session can proactively replace its codes
with `POST /auth/recovery/rotate` and an empty `{}` body.

`POST /auth/password/reset` is deliberately **capture-mailbox only**. It
consumes an email-code challenge and changes a password only when the
email-code and local-password identities already belong to the same principal.
Production refuses with `SNAPBACK_AUTH_PASSWORD_RESET_UNAVAILABLE`; it is not a
stand-in for mail delivery. Production signup is likewise reported unready in
`authProgramReadiness.passwordProvider` and refuses with
`SNAPBACK_AUTH_PASSWORD_SIGNUP_UNAVAILABLE` until blind-accept delivery exists.

### Mint a local session from a trusted server

The paved local operation is
`snapback session mint --email <address> --ready-file <path>`. A trusted broker
that cannot invoke the CLI may call the same host operation over HTTP. The
canonical [exact request, response, authority, and refusal contract](../operating/host-ops.md#mint-a-session-over-http)
lives with the host-ops surface so its shapes have one home. Adopt the returned
bearer through the first-party external-session custody path instead of
inventing another auth carrier. Keep both header values and the returned token
in trusted server custody. Never run this request in browser/native application
code, bake its secrets into a bundle, or treat the non-production gate as
hosted identity.

Two more session routes are shipped and deliberately narrow.
`POST /auth/step-up/request` mints a five-minute, operation-bound
re-authentication challenge for authority-creating consent (approving an
agent grant can demand one via `SNAPBACK_AUTH_STEP_UP_REQUIRED`); its code
delivery shares the mailbox boundary above — on a deployment profile without
the capture mailbox there is no delivery path until LLP 0045's mail adapter
exists, and the request refuses with
`SNAPBACK_AUTH_STEP_UP_DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE`. `POST /auth/family-alarm` is
the opaque, revoke-only alarm for a bearer you believe leaked: it revokes the
still-live session behind the presented bearer's token family and returns a
deliberately delayed, uniform, empty response, so it cannot be used to probe
which bearers are live.

## A browser app under sessions today

There is no production email delivery yet, so a real end user in a browser
cannot receive a sign-in code from the shipped provider — "email-code login,
React web" has no self-serve path today. The mailbox recipe above is
local-test material (admin- and impersonation-gated; never in a browser
bundle). What a web author actually does today is one of these:

- **Dev mode** (`auth: { mode: 'dev' }`) for the authoring loop — trusted
  client-passed `userId`, no sign-in UI at all. Browser requests may carry
  that selector from the Snapback listener's own origin or an exact loopback
  origin listed in `SNAPBACK_DEV_AUTH_ORIGINS` (comma-separated); another
  localhost port is refused with `SNAPBACK_AUTH_DEV_ORIGIN_REFUSED`. The
  supervised Expo loop registers its Metro origin automatically, and the
  standard Vite composition uses the same-origin `/__snapback` relay. Curl,

<!-- since: 0.1.9 -->

requires declared custody. The paved path declares **anonymous-public**
custody, which sends the protocol offer with no credential:

```js source=packages/snapback-client/app-data.test.mjs

```

The custody is mutually exclusive with browser, agent, and external-bearer
custody: passing a bearer alongside it throws rather than silently
downgrading, so no caller-selected identity can be smuggled through the
anonymous path. Anonymous clients read `public` queries only; protected
queries refuse exactly as they do for a signed-out browser.

For a non-session **admin/inspection** client against a sessions-mode server,
pass both options together. `authClientProtocol: 1` satisfies the server's
protocol-offer gate; without it the server refuses
`SNAPBACK_AUTH_PROFILE_CLIENT_UNSUPPORTED`. `custody: 'anonymous-public'`
satisfies the client constructor; `authClientProtocol: 1` alone throws a
custody `TypeError`. Each refusal names one half; this is the complete pair:

```js source=packages/snapback-client/app-data.test.mjs
